worked_solution:
The $3$rd row of the matrix contains two zeros, more than any other row. So using a Laplace expansion along the $3$rd row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & 6 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & -5 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{31}+(-5)\cdot {C}_{32}+(-5)\cdot {C}_{33}+0\cdot {C}_{34} \\  & =(-5)\cdot (-1)^{3+2}|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & -4 & 1 \\ -1 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}|+(-5)\cdot (-1)^{3+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -3 \\ 3 & 6 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =5\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & -4 & 1 \\ -1 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}|-5\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -3 \\ 3 & 6 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$
